title: Projects under a budget, crews and regional caps

blocks.text: This is the screen's whiteboard, coded. A telecom operator chooses tower upgrades: each has a `cost` ($k), `crew` weeks, a `region` and a `value`. `upgrades.py` already has one binary per project and the objective, the most value. Write `add_rules(model, x, projects, limits)` with every rule:

items: the total cost is at most `limits.budget`, and the total crew-weeks at most `limits.crew`;
at most `limits.region_cap[r]` projects in each region `r`; a region with no entry in `limits.region_cap` has no cap;
for each pair in `limits.conflicts`, not both;
for each pair `(a, b)` in `limits.needs`, `a` only if `b`.

blocks.text: Write the formulation first (sets, parameters, variables with domains, labelled rows with quantifiers). The tests fix plans and ask HiGHS whether the model accepts them, so any correct formulation passes. About ten lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Project:
    pid: str
    cost: int            # $k
    crew: int            # crew-weeks
    region: str
    value: int = 0


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Limits:
    budget: int
    crew: int
    region_cap: dict[str, int]
    conflicts: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)   # not both
    needs: list[tuple[str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)       # (a, b): a only if b


def add_rules(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, projects: list[Project], limits: Limits) -> None:
    """Budget, crew-weeks, a cap per region, conflicting pairs and needs."""
    # TODO: the rows of your formulation.
    return None


def build(projects: list[Project], limits: Limits) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="tower-upgrades")
    x = {p.pid: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{p.pid}") for p in projects}
    add_rules(model, x, projects, limits)
    model.maximize(sum(p.value * x[p.pid] for p in projects))
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    model, x = build([Project("A", 40, 3, "N", 10), Project("B", 30, 2, "N", 8)], Limits(60, 4, {"N": 1}))
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS)
    print(result.termination.reason.name, result.objective_value())

cases.says: a plan within the budget is allowed, and one over it refused
a plan that needs more crew-weeks than there are is refused
a region with more projects than its cap is refused
two conflicting projects together are refused
a needed project may be funded alone, and the one that needs it may not
projects in different regions count against different caps
a region missing from the caps has no cap, and a region with a cap still has one
